comparison: Perfect alignment on clustering analysis (C9, C56-C59, C61-C64, C83-C84). Both evaluations find the clustering approach valid and well-supported. OpenEval notes appropriate critical analysis of exceptions; peer reviewers explicitly validated the clustering methodology and confirmed validation approaches produced significant results.

Complete agreement on C31. Both evaluations accept the negative control result showing reduced performance with enhancer-based regions. This finding supports the methodological choice to use differentially open chromatin regions.

Perfect alignment on quality control validation (C78-C79). Both evaluations accept the dinucleotide patterns as evidence of proper nucleosome positioning. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly praised the precise dyad position identification as a strength.

Complete agreement on limitations (C66-C74). Both evaluations view the acknowledgment of computational and data limitations positively. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly stated authors did a good job describing limitations, aligning with OpenEval's assessment of appropriate scientific rigor.

Significant disagreement on context-dependent PTF behavior (C25-C28, C30). OpenEval finds the Yamanaka factor results internally consistent and well-supported. Peer Reviewer 3 raises fundamental concerns about low reproducibility, high dependence on anchor cell type selection, and criticizes removal of Yamanaka factor labels as hiding computational framework issues.

Agreement on NCAP-SELEX validation (C32-C33, C55). Both evaluations accept the correlation with experimental data as appropriate validation. OpenEval notes the trend was not statistically significant due to limited data; peer reviewers found the validation approach produced reasonable, trending results.

Partial overlap with strong agreement. OpenEval evaluates broader method development (C6-C7, C22-C24, C81); peer review focuses on statistical validation (C22-C24). Both find evidence solid and validation successful, with peer reviewers noting the enrichment score performs well in identifying known PTFs.

Partial overlap on computational approach (C6-C7). Both evaluations affirm the methodological framework. Peer reviewers described methods as straightforward and easy to interpret with precise nucleosome dyad identification. OpenEval evaluates broader validation including C22-C24, C81 not covered in this peer result.

Substantial overlap on PTF predictions (C8, C34-C35, C38-C39, C82). Both evaluations support the findings. Peer reviewers note identification of novel PTFs and validation of known PTFs, though Reviewer 2 raised uncertainty about expression consideration across cell types. OpenEval also covers literature validation (C36-C37, C40-C43) addressed separately in peer R5.

Covers literature-based validation portion (C36-C37, C40-C43) of OpenEval R2. Both evaluations accept literature citations as appropriate validation. Peer reviewers noted multiple validation approaches produced significant or reasonable results without challenging the literature support.

Strong agreement on correlation analysis and dual-nature TFs (C44-C48). Both evaluations accept the motif density-nucleosome occupancy correlation approach. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly validated this methodology and noted it produced significant results. The dual nature interpretation was not challenged.

Agreement on cell-type-specific CTCF activity (C52-C53). Both evaluations support this finding. Peer reviewers accepted it without challenge, noting alignment with prior literature. OpenEval covers broader correlation analysis (C44-C51) while peer review focuses specifically on CTCF result.

Disagreement on interpretation of C65 and C81. OpenEval finds the mechanistic interpretation about chromatin opening and reprogramming potential reasonable and supported. Peer Reviewer 3 raises fundamental concerns about reproducibility and cell-type dependency, suggesting the interpretation may be overstated despite Reviewer 1 accepting improved classification accuracy.

OpenEval evaluates the central hypothesis (C20-C21) as reasonable and validated by subsequent results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not explicitly assess the hypothesis formulation itself.

OpenEval evaluates scientific background and motivation (C1-C5, C10-C19) as well-supported by literature and accurately representing current knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not explicitly assess background claims.

OpenEval evaluates broader significance context (C75-C77) regarding PTF therapeutics and established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not explicitly assess these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates C80 regarding PTF-nucleosome interaction complexity as supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not explicitly assess this background claim.
